summary: Nora can now raise a note about something a conversation left open, after the fact. Reviewing a finished turn, she can spot an unresolved question nobody was tracking and write it down where it will be found again.
details: She raises one only when she can say what would settle it and when it happened. Most turns raise nothing, and that is the expected answer.
She will not raise a note about something the turn already opened and set aside. The two paths would otherwise argue about the same note every turn, forever.

A note she gets wrong — a title too long, no date, nothing that would close it — is refused rather than trimmed to fit. The list of open questions is only useful if it is complete, and a silent trim loses something nobody can see is gone.
Nothing about a note going wrong costs the running summary of the conversation. That is what she reads on her next turn; a note is not.
limitations: She does not revise existing notes here. Reading one and editing it during a turn is already hers; tidying across notes belongs to the background pass.

If she raises a note about something an existing note already covers, both exist. Merging them is the background pass's job, and two visible notes are recoverable in a way one silently absorbing the other is not.
